title: vps rename JSON
description: Payload of `ssh-cli vps rename <NAME> <NEW_NAME> --json` and of `vps edit <NAME> --name <NEW>`. A rename moves the registry key, the record name field and, when it points at this host, the sibling active marker. Stored credentials stay readable under the new name: the record serializes them without associated data, so opening a blob never needs the name it was stored under. The ciphertext token itself is resealed with a fresh nonce on every save, which is ordinary AEAD behavior and never touches the plaintext. Every invocation reports target_source `argv`, because this verb requires the subject on its own command line and never reads the active marker.

name.description: Name the host answers to after this invocation

previous_name.description: Name the host answered to before this invocation. Present so an agent never has to remember what it asked for.

active_rewritten.description: True when the sibling active marker pointed at `previous_name` and was rewritten to `name`; false when it pointed at another host or was absent, in which case it was left untouched.

updated.description: Fields whose stored value changed, in application order, each at most once. Empty when the invocation only renamed the host; a rename that also edited fields lists them, which only `vps edit --name` can do. Always present.

target_resolved.description: Name the registry lookup used, which is the name the host had before this invocation, so it always equals `previous_name` and never the new `name`. Published only after the registry lookup succeeded, so a not-found error carries no resolved target.

target_source.description: Always `argv`: the target came from the invocation itself.
